sections.overview: Labeo altivelis Peters, 1852 is a freshwater cyprinid of the genus Labeo, native to the Zambezi and upper Congo basins.
sections.identification: It reaches about 49 centimetres total length and has a conspicuously tall, sail-like dorsal fin with 14–16 soft rays.
sections.habitat: Adults favour large rivers but also inhabit large lakes and reservoirs, including Lake Malawi and Lake Mweru.
sections.diet: It grazes algae and aufwuchs, the film of organisms growing on submerged rocks.
sections.behavior: Adults make seasonal, potamodromous migrations from Lake Moëro into the Luapula system to spawn.
sections.reproduction: Spawning occurs in a short, concentrated event during the river ascent, locally known as kapata in the Luapula–Moëro system.
sections.ecology: Recent genomic work shows that traditional Labeo groupings do not always represent evolutionary lineages; the companion profiles of L. rosae and L. ruddi allow comparison of their ranges and habitats.
sections.conservation: A recent IUCN freshwater-fish summary lists it as globally Least Concern, with population trend unknown.
